body.statement: The constructed set \(\mathcal B_{\mathrm{des}}\) is finite, \(\mathcal C_\kappa=\mathcal C_\infty\) for every \(\kappa>K\), and, whenever \(\Theta(P)\ne\varnothing\), \(U(P)<+\infty\) if and only if \(P\notin\mathcal C_\infty\), equivalently if and only if \(D_\infty(P)>0\). Moreover, \(\Theta(P)\) is relatively open in \([0,+\infty)\), is a finite union of intervals, and every finite upper endpoint lies in \(\mathcal B_{\mathrm{des}}\) and is not attained. Enumerating all price strata and deciding the finite semialgebraic feasibility systems recovers the exact set and its upper endpoint without a monotonicity presumption.
body.justification: The theorem gives the exact observable finite-ceiling criterion for the maintained subclass.  Its terminal rationalization and hence the infinite-ceiling direction transfer to any containing class, whereas terminal exclusion does not transfer upward by subclass inclusion alone.
body.gap: Pakes et al. obtain common-menu moment-inequality bounds and state that their nonparametric changing-menu inequalities do not deliver an upper bound; neither they nor Mbakop characterize upper-tail saturation under turnover.
body.consumer: The health-choice application can retain year pairs crossing plan entry or exit precisely when the observed path table is separated from the terminal body.
body.proof_tex:
There are finitely many deterministic response tables, and every comparison multigraph has finitely many directed simple cycles.  By \(\texttt{def:comparison-graph}\), each cycle weight is
\[
 W_C(\kappa)=A_C+B_C\kappa,
\]
where \(A_C\in\mathbb Q\) and \(B_C\in\mathbb Z\).  Each affine function with \(B_C\ne0\) has at most one root.  Hence adjoining zero to all nonnegative roots produces a finite rational set \(\mathcal B_{\mathrm{des}}\), and \(K=\max\mathcal B_{\mathrm{des}}\) is finite and rational.

Fix \(\kappa>K\).  If \(B_C>0\), then \(W_C(\kappa)>0\): when its root is nonnegative this follows from \(\kappa>K\), and when its root is negative it follows for every nonnegative \(\kappa\).  If \(B_C=0\), positivity is equivalent to \(A_C>0\).  If \(B_C<0\), the weight is negative to the right of a nonnegative root, or throughout the nonnegative half-line when its root is negative.  Therefore
\[
 W_C(\kappa)>0\text{ for every simple cycle }C
 \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
 \bigl[B_C>0\text{ or }(B_C=0\text{ and }A_C>0)\bigr]
 \text{ for every }C.
\]
By \(\texttt{lem:strict-cycle-feasibility}\) and \(\texttt{def:terminal-body}\), this is exactly
\[
 F_\kappa=F_\infty\qquad(\kappa>K).
\]
The quadratic map and convex-hull construction are then identical, so \(\texttt{thm:sharp-iid-body}\) yields
\[
 \mathcal C_\kappa=\mathcal C_\infty\qquad(\kappa>K).
\]

Assume \(\Theta(P)\ne\varnothing\), as required by \(\texttt{ass:correct-specification}\).  If \(P\in\mathcal C_\infty\), the preceding equality gives \((K,+\infty)\subseteq\Theta(P)\), hence \(U(P)=+\infty\).  If \(P\notin\mathcal C_\infty\), no \(\kappa>K\) belongs to \(\Theta(P)\); its nonempty identified set is bounded above by \(K\), so \(U(P)<+\infty\).  Compactness of \(\mathcal C_\infty\), supplied by the sharp-body theorem applied to \(F_\infty\), implies that its complement has strictly positive distance.  Therefore
\[
 U(P)<+\infty
 \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
 P\notin\mathcal C_\infty
 \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
 D_\infty(P)>0.
\]

Suppose \(P\in\mathcal C_{\kappa_0}\).  By the sharp-body theorem it has a finite representation using response laws \(q^\ell\).  Only finitely many response tables have positive weight.  Every simple-cycle weight for each such table is strictly positive at \(\kappa_0\); continuity of finitely many affine functions gives a relative neighborhood of \(\kappa_0\) in \([0,+\infty)\) on which all remain positive.  The same \(q^\ell\) and outer mixing weights therefore represent \(P\) throughout that neighborhood.  Hence \(\Theta(P)\) is relatively open.

Removing \(\mathcal B_{\mathrm{des}}\) partitions \([0,+\infty)\) into finitely many open strata.  On each stratum no cycle weight changes sign, so \(F_\kappa\), \(\mathcal C_\kappa\), and the membership decision for \(P\) are constant.  Relative openness rules out isolated compatible breakpoints.  It follows that \(\Theta(P)\) is a finite union of relatively open intervals.  Every finite upper endpoint is a stratum boundary in \(\mathcal B_{\mathrm{des}}\), and relative openness shows that it is not attained.

For a fixed enumerated response set \(F\), membership has the explicit finite semialgebraic certificate
\[
\begin{gathered}
 w_\ell\ge0,\qquad \sum_{\ell=1}^{m}w_\ell=1,
 \qquad q_{\ell f}\ge0,\qquad \sum_{f\in F}q_{\ell f}=1,\\
 P_{ab}=\sum_{\ell=1}^{m}w_\ell
 \left(\sum_{f\in F}q_{\ell f}\mathbf 1\{f_1=a\}\right)
 \left(\sum_{f\in F}q_{\ell f}\mathbf 1\{f_2(a)=b\}\right)
 \quad(a\in M_1,b\in M_2).
\end{gathered}
\]
All coefficients are rational, all variables and constraints are displayed, and the bound of \(m\) outer components was proved above.  A finite exact sign-decomposition procedure applies: project successively using the finitely many coefficients, discriminants, and pairwise resultants in the last variable; isolate the resulting univariate real roots by signed polynomial-remainder sequences and rational isolating intervals; and lift one sign-invariant cell at a time.  The number of variables falls at every projection step, while every lift has finitely many algebraic boundary roots, so the recursion terminates and returns either an algebraic feasible point or the finite list of sign-invariant cells certifying infeasibility.  Testing one representative of each open price stratum and each breakpoint value with this certified procedure therefore recovers every interval of \(\Theta(P)\); the largest compatible stratum boundary is the exact finite value of \(U(P)\).  This search does not presume nesting or monotonicity in \(\kappa\).

Finally, let \(\mathfrak M_{\mathrm{ac}}\) denote the maintained absolutely continuous fixed-cell subclass and let \(\mathfrak M_{\mathrm{pub}}\) be any broader published fixed-cell class containing it.  When \(P\in\mathcal C_\infty\), the sharp-body construction supplies, for every \(\kappa>K\), a rationalizing law inside \(\mathfrak M_{\mathrm{ac}}\); the conclusion \(U(P)=+\infty\) therefore transfers upward to \(\mathfrak M_{\mathrm{pub}}\) by subclass inclusion.  In contrast, \(P\notin\mathcal C_\infty\) excludes only laws covered by the necessity argument for \(\mathfrak M_{\mathrm{ac}}\).  Nonmembership in a subclass-generated body is not, by set inclusion alone, an exclusion certificate for a larger class, so the finite-ceiling direction does not transfer upward without separately proving necessity for that larger class.
